Dartaxâgerdim (F22)

Region (English scoring-table division): Bulwar.

In one sentence: An old human Sun Cult state that broke free from a Sun Elf kingdom must redefine Bulwari light between revenge and reconstruction.

Story: High｜Mission-tree length: Medium-long (41 direct F22 missions)｜Mission-tree update: use the local scripts supporting EU4 v1.37.5.0｜Uniqueness: High｜Tedium: Medium (multi-front wars and institutional construction)｜Early pressure: High｜Expansion ability: High

Identity and History

Dartaxâgerdim is a human monarchy in Bahar in 1444, following the Old Bulwari Sun Cult. The history script gives it Dartaxes as ruler, Tailmaz as heir, a historical rivalry with Birsartanšes and a friendship with Reuyel. It is not a unified Bulwar empire, but a rebel state shaped by Sun Elf rule, religious persecution and regional wars. [Local history script]

The offline English Wiki's Akalate of Dartaxâgerdim says that it broke away from Birsartanšes in 1428 during the Decades of Devastation, and that the new state built the Garlas-kel Palace of Magi in the ruins of an ancient djinn palace. This prehistory is compatible with the 1444 starting identity, but the Wiki's successor name does not mean that the player must later be destroyed or change Tag. [Wiki]

National Story and Campaign Arc

The early campaign is a human revolt against Sun Elf hegemony and a war to recover Bahari lands. The mission text includes sheltering displaced people and commemorating those killed for the Old Sun Cult, but it also includes Green Helmet assassinations, hatred and raiding. The conflict is not simply “humans good, elves evil”: after overthrowing one form of oppression, the state must decide whether it will create another through fanaticism. [Local flavour text]

The middle game turns toward magic and governance. Human magical knowledge has weakened under Sun Elf rule and war; the missions recruit mage refugees, rebuild Houses of Wisdom, investigate djinn relics and develop Wish magic. Religiously, “Diversity is Strength” resists compressing every Old Sun Cult local tradition into one doctrine. At the same time, missions involving the secret Serpent King cult, mage power and religious families force the player to manage another risk of elite monopoly. [Local flavour text]

Core Mechanics and Route

The first loop is conquest and reconstruction in Bahar and Bulwar: take cities in war, then turn the legacy of war into a governable heartland. The second is a magical revival: the history script already gives the mage estate a privileged place, while the missions connect mage loyalty, academies, djinn ruins, special resources and spellcraft. The third is religious politics: coexistence among Old Sun Cult sects or the influence of radical sects changes the character of the state rather than supplying an ordinary religious bonus. [Local script]

F22 has two distinct successor choices. The current formation decisions can establish Surakes (F52) under one set of conditions or Mushasharām (F53) under another; both change Tag and mission tree, and the F53 route prevents forming F52 later. “Baharšes” is a country-name override used by F22's missions, not a third independent Tag. The decisions have specific territory, building and flag requirements; neither successor should be written as an empire that exists at the start. [Local script]

Personality and Recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 88/100｜Autocracy 78/100｜Magic↔Artifice 86/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 75/100)｜Pluralism 58/100.

The v2.1 values profile is Neutral (58/100) with a mixed trajectory. Sheltering refugees, rebuilding Bahar and respecting local Old Sun Cult traditions serve the public good; Green Helmet assassinations and collective hatred of Sun Elves reduce dignity and restraint. Conquest and monarchy are not scored as moral negatives by themselves. The route suits players who enjoy religious revolution, Bulwari wars, djinn and mage legacies, and multiple formable-country choices. It is not a relaxed campaign if you dislike intense warfare, complicated religious infighting or a rebellion story with moral shadows.

Community Experience and Evidence Boundary

Dev Diary 41 explicitly discusses the tree's rework, the Green Helmets and its mage themes. Player posts often praise the long wars leading from Dartaxâgerdim toward Baharšes and Surakes, but these are older-version experiences and do not establish current formation conditions. [Official dev diary] [Community view]

Exact script lines, Wiki revision data and community sources are recorded in the evidence page. The 1454 retreat and 1484 end shown in the Halann map are secondary research and another historical line; they are not presented as the player's inevitable future.

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here; suspicious percentages or script-valued effects require separate review. Raw script values are shown where appropriate.

Dartaxâgerdi Traditions

  • Infantry combat ability: +10% (infantry_power; raw value 0.1).

  • morale_damage_received: -10% (morale_damage_received; raw value -0.1).

1. Dartaxes of Farramaz

The legacy of few individuals in recent Bulwari history is as divisive as that of Dartaxes szel-Farramaz. Born in 1401 AA to a minor Barkabti noble family hailing from Farramaz, then one of the northern provinces of Birzartanšes, he spent his youth at court in Birsartansbar. Showing a talent for command and an aptitude for military strategy, he rose to the rank of general at the tender age of eighteen. Proving his mettle against enemy forces during the Baharkandi-Birsartanšesi War, his exceptional victory at the battle of Habqez cemented his reputation. This would prove to be a mixed blessing, however, as he received the thankless task of subduing the Great Rebellion and reestablishing order in the northern provinces ravaged by the Decades of Devastation. But loyal service to inept monarch is seldom rewarded, leading to a deep estrangement and the eventual rebellion of Dartaxes himself, who gathered an unlikely coalition of soldiers loyal to him, provincial nobles with connections to his family, and, most importantly, the fanatically devout Šebhuliam sect. While he failed to overthrow Arantir of Birzartanšes, he managed to forge his own realm out of the borderlands between Birzartanšes and Baharkand. Many hopes were pinned upon him, the first independent human Akal in Bahar since the fall of the Phoenix Empire. Yet it all came crashing down when in 1484 the forces of Birzartanšes reconquered this fledgling realm and he was burned alive in the ruins of the Šebhuliam fortress of Azka-szel-Parkellu.

  • Legitimacy: +0.5 (legitimacy; raw value 0.5).

  • Devotion: +0.5 (devotion; raw value 0.5).

  • Horde unity: +0.5 (horde_unity; raw value 0.5).

2. The Magi of Lake Garles

For several millennia, the seemingly tranquil lake Garlas hid an astounding secret beneath the salt pans along its shores. Buried beneath the surface lie the ruins of Is-Kuršag, one of the four capitals of the djinni Radiant Sultanates. Its rediscovery during the mid-15th century AA led to the establishment of an Eka, a bulwari mage academy devoted to the study of genie magic which developed into one of the foremost institutions of bulwari magic as a whole. This Eka-Uššupammun, or ‘Palace whose Foundations Hide Knowledge’ swiftly became one of the major support pillars of Dartaxâgerdim and survived its downfall by seeking shelter under the wings of a resurgent harpy queendom that took over the mountainous eastern provinces of the akalate. Mages trained within these walls tend to swiftly rise to prestigious positions and often become revered masters of the arcane arts. Yet without fail they refuse to divulge details of their time spend at the Eka to outsiders, lending it an air of mystery and igniting the imagination of conspiracy theorists across Bulwar, who speculate about everything from a secret cabal of genie cultists ruling over the academy to a hidden gate to the elemental plane of air or the incorporeal spirits of several god-kings trapped in a wishblade stored in the catacombs of the Eka.

  • Shock damage: +10% (shock_damage; raw value 0.1).

3. Lessons of the Great Rebellion

The Decades of Devastation, as the name implies, had a catastrophic effect on the lands of Bahar. Like a corroding acid the constant border skirmishes, rampant banditry and open neglect of infrastructure and institutions alike led to a dissolution of societal structures once thought inviolate. Not only the people of Bahar struggled to cling to a semblance of normalcy, trying to earn their livelyhood while armies clashed all around them. Those armies themselves suffered from the rampant institutional collapse as well, lacking secure supply lines and reliable access to the necessary Tools of their bloody trade. One of the often overlooked aspects of Dartaxes’ military genius was therefore his astute understanding of logistics and the development of an ingeniously flexible supply system primarily based on local sympathizers and supplemented by the remnants of the old Birsartanšesi military administration that he suborned for his purposes.

  • Manpower recovery speed: +10% (manpower_recovery_speed; raw value 0.10).

4. The Green Helmets

‘The light does not cower from the dark, it dispels all shadow and burns away all falsehood - how can you consider yourself devoted to Surakel's Light if you are unwilling to follow the example He set and stride forth to vanquish the Malevolent Dark!’ -Fragment of a Šebhuliam harangue

The Šebhuliam were founded by Ašuru Telissaku, son of a preacher from the Cult of Mourning called Xakkim. After the Purge of Medurubar, Ašuru and his father fled north. While Xakkim’s followers became the Cult of Purity, Ašuru and his acolytes built the fortress of Azka-szel-Parkellu, the ‘Fortress of those who seek Purity’, in the mountain of Kuzak over the ruins of the harpy roost of Tounafira. His followers became the Green Helmets, a moniker referring to their habit of tying green cloth as a symbol of faithful purity around their helmets when they left their mountain fastness on their initiation missions to assassinate sun elven officials or other proponents of the New Sun Cult.

  • Missionary strength against heretics: +2% (global_heretic_missionary_strength; raw value 0.02).

  • War score cost against other religions: -15% (warscore_cost_vs_other_religion; raw value -0.15).

5. The Cult of Purity

Bulwar has no lack of tragedies in its long history. One of the more recent ones gave rise to the Cult of Purity. The Purge of Medurubar was a massacre of recalcitrant adherents of sun cults that rejected the doctrinal consensus reached at the council of Brasan. Originally a shelter for those who rejected the theological reforms pushed through by Taelarios and his allies amongst the clergy, the city of Medurubar soon became a target for the more zealous adherents of the new status quo. The adherents of the Cult of Mourning, a cult risen in the wake of the destruction wrought by the Red Xhaz all along the lower Suran, were among those who hoped to practice their faith undisturbed within the walls of Medurubar. Once the Order of the Zenith raised their blades to purge Medurubar from heresy, only few managed to escape the massacre. One of these survivors was the preacher Xakkim and his followers, who fled north into the wilderness of the Šad Kuz and into Bahar, where they founded the Cult of Purity, whose central doctrine is the concept that the people of Bulwar have to endure tragedies and suffering due to the spiritual corruption of Surakel’s Garden, and that only by ritually cleansing it may it thrive again. Aside from the Cult of Mourning, other venerable cults native to Bahar such as the Cult of Truth or the Cult of the Mother have influenced the Genesis of the Cult of Purity, which in turn birthed the Green Helmets or Šebhuliam.

  • True faith tolerance: +2 (tolerance_own; raw value 2).

6. The City of Uak

Modesty, restraint or low self-esteem are not character traits commonly associated with gnollish rulers, and Uak ‘the Tremendous’ was no exception. He did not waste any time once his pack had carved out a sizable chunk of Bahar for their new kingdom and began to work on his legacy by founding a new city on the banks of the Našra to serve as his capital. With typical gnollish bluntness and flair for self-aggrandizing he named this city Akal-Uakbar - the City of King Uak. Over the many centuries since its founding, that name has been shortened to Akal-Uak. Unlike most other major Bulwari cities that are found on the flat floodplains of major rivers, Akal-Uak stretches across several hills, with each hill being the center of a city-within-the city, a last remnant of gnollish tendencies to place some distance between sub-packs within a large gnollish horde to avoid unnecessary conflict born from rivalries or mere boredom. For the longest time Akal-Uak has been the undisputed hegemon of the Našra valley, and perennial rival of Aqatbar for the title of capital of Bahar. Only in the last centuries it had to cede its preeminent role to Birsartansbar. It comes as no surprise then, that the aristocrats of Akal-Uak were quick to throw their support behind Dartaxes when he first secured the city and its environs for his master after the first battle of Habqez, and became its true king after defeating Arantir of Birsartanšes in the second battle of Habqez, turning it into the capital of his newborn akalate after the successful Great Rebellion.

  • Stability cost modifier: -20% (stability_cost_modifier; raw value -0.2).

7. Tealwood Amber

The gnollish pack of Uak, like those of his compatriots, brought suffering and despair to Surakel's Garden, but that is not all they brought. Uak carried with him a memento of his homeland on the other side of the Salahad, a couple of Hašitu seedlings, or Tealwood trees as the Cannorians call them. Planted in a sheltered valley near Akal-Uak, they formed a large Tealwood forest over time - the last of its kind as the lands these trees hailed from were swallowed by the Shadow Swamp in the centuries that have passed since.

Local artisans have long known that the sap collected from these trees hardens into a teal coloured amber when exposed to air and sunlight and built a thriving industry around it. This Tealwood amber is surprisingly pliant in the hands of skilled artists and intricate jewelry as well as small sculptures crafted from it are highly sought after all across Bulwar and beyond.

  • Production efficiency: +10% (production_efficiency; raw value 0.10).
